findings.mechanism: Cache stores every distinct query result forever, causing memory usage to grow linearly with query diversity.
findings.remediation: Add a size limit and eviction policy to the cache, removing oldest entries when limit exceeded.
findings.arithmetic: 2000 queries * 5 results per query * ~1KB per result ≈ 10,000,000 bytes

findings.mechanism: CPU‑intensive token verification runs in the event loop of a single uvicorn worker, limiting throughput and causing request latency to grow when request rate exceeds the worker’s processing capacity.
findings.remediation: Move token verification to a thread pool or reduce _ROUNDS, and increase the number of uvicorn workers.
findings.arithmetic: Assume each verification takes ~20 ms; a single worker can handle ~50 req/s. At 50 req/s the queue length grows, leading to p99 latency > 1000 ms.

findings.mechanism: The global _entries dict is accessed from multiple async requests without synchronization, risking race conditions and corrupted cache state under concurrent access.
findings.remediation: Guard all accesses to _entries with a threading.Lock or replace with a thread‑safe cache implementation.
findings.arithmetic: Concurrent requests can interleave reads/writes; risk appears as soon as >1 request overlaps.

findings.mechanism: Each request opens a new SQLite connection; SQLite allows only one writer at a time, so concurrent writes block readers, increasing latency and possibly causing timeouts.
findings.remediation: Use a shared connection or a connection pool and enable WAL mode to allow concurrent reads.
findings.arithmetic: With N concurrent writers, readers wait up to the default 5 s timeout; latency grows proportionally to writer count.

findings.mechanism: Search loads all document rows and filters in Python, causing query cost to scale with total document count, leading to latency spikes as the dataset grows.
findings.remediation: Add an index on terms and perform filtered query in SQL instead of scanning all rows.
findings.arithmetic: If documents = D, time ≈ O(D); with D=10000, expected latency >200 ms.
